predecessors.name: Mughal Empire
predecessors.text: Baroda and the hill fort of Songadh in south Gujarat

successors.name: Republic of India
successors.text: the four prants Kadi, Baroda, Navsari and Amreli, with Okhamandal and Kodinar on the Kathiawar coast: several disjointed tracts

ledger.x: 1721: Pilaji Gaekwad conquers Songadh from the Mughals and the Baroda State is founded.

ledger.cp: holder of Kodinar parganah (not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1 February 1940: the Attachment Scheme begins with Pethapur and adds territory to Baroda until 1943.
1 May 1949: Baroda merges into the Dominion of India.

wars.name: Third Battle of Panipat
wars.outcome: Damaji Gaekwad fought in the Maratha army that was beaten at Panipat; no Gaekwad territory changed.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: Baroda fought on the British side (listed among the British-side belligerents) and, per the Baroda State page, "acknowledged British suzerainty" after the war; its own borders did not move.

certainty.note: Revenue-collecting districts and tributes in Gujarat; the pages give towns and prants, not boundaries.

Four prants and the parganah of Kodinar are recorded administrative units; the tracts are scattered ("several disjointed tracts") and drawn as circles around their towns, so the drawn edge is approximate.
